answer: Each identity must complete a fresh, prescribed sequence of modular squarings, with each result depending on the previous one; a Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the work efficiently. GPUs cannot parallelize a single chain to remove its elapsed-time requirement, though they can run separate chains concurrently. Thus clones require additional sequential work and hardware—a bottleneck, not an absolute ban on parallelism, like moving a marble past a falcon through a grove one step at a time.
